newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares extend climb for third day, volume up.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares extend climb for third day, volume up.

text.p: Greek equities continued their advance for the third consecutive day as trading volume jumped to 11 billion drachmas. Brokers said further gains could unfold as the market was discounting a strong government after the elections.

"The market looked strong with players discounting a cohesive government after the elections regardless of the result. That's what it reads. Stocks could climb further to 960-970 points on the benchmark index," said broker Nick Stathopoulos at N.Devletoglou Securities.
"There has been a net inflow of funds and we had very good trading volume at 11 billion drachmas. If this continues stocks will head higher," he said.
Greece will hold early elections September 22.

The Athens general share index closed 0.64 percent, or 6.01 points higher at 944.61 from Wednesday's 938.60 close after opening at 939.29 points. Turnover rose to 11.01 billion drachmas from 9.21 billion on Wednesday on volume of 5.93 million shares.

There were block trades in Alte, Viohalko, Etem and OTE telecom. Advancers led decliners 125 to 76 with 40 issues unchanged on 241 traded. Banks gained 0.80 percent, industrials advanced 0.71 percent and construction climbed 1.03 percent. Small-caps firmed 0.35 percent.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 559-577 at the close. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, ended higher 10 drachmas at 4,055.

The recently launched Merrill Lynch stock index call warrant based on a basket of 23 shares was quoted higher at 204.20-214.90 drachmas. It expires on January 9 1998 with a strike price of 1000. It was in the money at 1034.5.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 3,930-4,100 drachmas at the close. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
